{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the fish concept and sketched it on the pad, defining the shape the whole table built: a big, simple outline with the start at the nose, two body lines running back, and a forked tail. The design was built to be recognizable from the outline alone and to fall from a single push. The final picture was 118 dominoes, all connected to the start, so the full fish was set up to fall.

Execution: I traced stroke 1, the top body line carrying the start domino, and stood a domino back up where it needed it. I inspected the top run, the tail and the notch several times and confirmed the whole fish was connected from the nose before the push. I kept the curves soft and the branches gentle, which suits how dominoes pass the fall.

Collaboration: I assigned each stroke by name so that every person had a piece and the strokes could be built in parallel. I answered joint questions quickly, agreed with Sofia's call that the tail tip needed no join, and told people to keep their hands off the finished corner so nothing got bumped before the push.

Leadership: I set the plan in the first minute, chose the animal, and coordinated the order of work. The upper tail waited until the top run was through, and I kept everyone informed of the status. I called the hands-off point once everything was verified, which protected the finished work through to the push.

I believe my share of the table's result was about 40 percent, given the concept, the sketch, the start line and the coordination, with the others building the remaining strokes.", "my_share_percent": 40}
